name: Flechte
prior: Lotka-Volterra in sound tools exists at audio rate and at composition level, not as the slow envelope/timbre law of a note. Audio rate: Fontana 2012 'Interactive sound synthesis by the Lotka-Volterra population model' - discrete-time LV as a real-time Pure Data Java external at 44.1 kHz (VS: air.uniud.it/handle/11390/902566, researchgate 274068940); PreyShaper VST3 waveshaper on the LV equations (VS: ittiawie.gumroad.com/l/preyshaper); Akihiko Matsumoto 'Lotka-Volterra' M4L, 'a feedback system at the edge of control' (VS: akihikomatsumoto.sellfy.store/p/ableton-lotka-volterra); Culto's Max gen~ patch of a two-species competition-cooperation LV model as synthesis (2022; VS: isotonikstudios.com culto); a VCV module 'Coalescent Bunnies' with LV / Rosenzweig-MacArthur predator-prey oscillator modes was named by one search summary of library.vcvrack.com but could not be confirmed (no hit on GitHub code search of the VCV manifests or in two further searches) - treat as unverified. Composition/ecosystem level: dreamfauna (Le Groux, CCRMA) - LV ecosystem over a fluid solver, creatures drive synth voices via OSC (VS: ccrma.stanford.edu/~slegroux dreamfauna); Living Symphonies (Jones & Bulley 2014) forest-ecosystem simulation driving a music engine (VS: thequietus.com/?p=15343); ixiQuarks 'Predators' SuperCollider ALife instrument (VS: quark.sccode.org/ixi/help/predators.html); Carlson's agent-based predator/prey sonification (VS: soundstudiesblog.com 2012/09/24, etheses.whiterose.ac.uk 15892). Named by the idea: Aalto drone machines, Make Noise Strega, Myzel's Nebel - different mechanisms (A). Not found: an instrument whose held notes are algae eaten by one shared fungus so that all fingers breathe together at a period set by light and finger count.
costNotes: Native, 8 nodes per voice: cached PeriodicWave oscillator (APP 3781) + lowpass + alga gain + noise BufferSource + 2 bandpass (f/2, f/4, Q 12-30) + fungus gain + out = about 0.35-0.45 units (0.03 per node, 0.06-0.1 per biquad; R: webaudio.md section 4); the idea's 0.45 is right. L3: 2 oscillators +-4 ct, 3 bandpass, panners = 0.75-0.85. The ODE runs in the main thread on the app's 25-ms worker tick (APP 6043) with two setTargetAtTime per voice per tick (tc 0.05) - negligible; clamp dt after a stall (background tab) or the Euler step jumps. Shared state A.fleP is one float. The decisive check is the dynamics, not the DSP (sim/bio2_sim.py): the specified system - logistic alga, linear predation c a p, predator growth e c abar p - has a globally stable coexistence point a* = m/(e c) = 0.533; its eigenvalues at y 0.5 are -0.27 +- 0.34 i with the parameters as written (c = 2.5 x 0.5, m = 0.8 x 0.5) and -0.27 +- 0.55 i if Biss/Hunger are read as absolute (c = 2.5, m = 0.8), i.e. a damped spiral with period 18 s / 11 s and e-folding 3.7 s (2.1 s at full light). Numerically: one swell (a 0.86 -> 0.48 -> 0.53) and then a flat drone at a = 0.533 for ever, identical with one or three fingers (the mean abar makes finger count irrelevant). Sustained breathing needs a Holling-II response (Rosenzweig-MacArthur, h = 1, m = 0.2): with the specified rates it cycles at 17-31 s; with all rates x3 the period is 5.8 s at y 1.0, 7.6 s at y 0.5, 10.3 s at y 0.2 - inside the 3-12 s target and light = period as intended - but the alga swings 0.03..0.66 (-27 dB dips), so gA needs a floor (~0.15) or a^0.5 compression; slow noise on the light (0.03 per tick, AR 0.98) keeps the cycle at 6.4-7.1 s with jitter (no LFO feel); Euler at dt 0.025 is accurate to 2 % (5.80 vs 5.67 s at dt 0.005). Alternative without a limit cycle: let Puls hits be periodic bites (forced oscillation at the lane's rate) - the damped system then breathes at the lane tempo, which is the idea's own 'Taktgeber des Atmens'.
soundHeld: As written, a held Flechte is Nebel with a slow swell: the alga blooms, gets bitten once (click, the sub-octave hiss rises), dims and settles at a constant level within ~20 s - the 'never repeating breathing' does not happen, verified by the ODE's eigenvalues and the simulation. With the Rosenzweig-MacArthur fix the held note becomes genuinely distinctive: a 6-10 s cycle of bright hollow bloom (partials 1,2,3,5,7 opening through the lowpass), a bite click as the alga collapses, a dark pitched fungus hiss at f/2 and f/4 swelling over the dying alga, then recovery - two actors in one note, shared across all fingers so chords breathe together, with light (Hoehe) setting the period 10 s -> 6 s. Risks: the cycle dips 27 dB (gaps of near-silence in a drone - floor it); a clean limit cycle sounds like an LFO after three repetitions (add slow light noise and let each new finger inject a bloom that resets the phase); the alga's periodic wave is a hollow organ next to Nebel/Obertoene/Tiefe, so the fungus band must be loud and the Biss click audible, or it is 'another drone'. First-10-seconds test: start a new note mid-cycle (a0 high, p low) so the first bite lands within 2-3 s.
soundBurst: A Puls hit (gate 0.22 s, burstEnv) is a short alga swell with a click - a soft organ blip, weak on its own, close to a Nebel burst. Its real value is feeding the shared fungus so the held notes of the same engine answer each hit with a bite: a lane as the breathing's metronome is a new cross-lane interaction and, with the damped ODE, the only way the system breathes at all (forced oscillation). Danger: a lane of 8ths feeds the fungus eight times per second, p saturates and every held alga is eaten to the floor - permanent dark hiss; cap the bite per hit and scale it by 1/sqrt(hit rate), or make p decay faster than the lane feeds it.
failureModes: The specified ODE does not oscillate: logistic prey + linear predation is a stable focus (eigenvalues -0.27 +- 0.34 i), one swell then a static drone - needs Holling-II / Rosenzweig-MacArthur with rates x3, a delay, or periodic forcing by Puls bites
Finger count does not change the period with abar = mean; use the sum of algae (more food = faster fungus) or per-finger bloom injection
Limit-cycle breathing dips to a = 0.03 (-27 dB) - near-silent holes in a drone; floor gA or compress
Clean limit cycle = LFO feel after three cycles; add slow noise on light and phase resets by new notes
Alga timbre (periodic wave through a lowpass) is a hollow organ next to Nebel/Obertoene/Tiefe; identity rests on the sub-octave fungus band and the bite click being loud enough
Shared fungus with a dense Puls lane saturates p and eats all held notes to the floor; cap and rate-scale the per-hit bite
Puls hit alone is a soft organ blip without a transient; the lane needs held Flechte notes to make sense
Main-thread tick stalls freeze the ODE; clamp dt on resume (the app's A.jitter exists, APP 6029-6031)
verdict: Rare: Lotka-Volterra is already in audio tools as an audio-rate oscillator or waveshaper (Fontana's Pd external 2012, PreyShaper VST3, Matsumoto's M4L, Culto's gen~ patch; a VCV predator-prey oscillator is reported but unconfirmed) and as ecosystem composition engines (dreamfauna, Living Symphonies, ixiQuarks Predators), but not as the slow envelope/timbre law of held notes with one fungus shared by all fingers. Native at about 0.4 units (L3 0.75), the 25-ms tick is free. The adversarial finding is in the maths, not the DSP: the ODE as written has a stable coexistence point (eigenvalues -0.27 +- 0.34 i), so a note swells once and then sits at a = 0.53 for ever, identical for one or three fingers - verified numerically; sustained 3-12 s breathing needs a Holling-II (Rosenzweig-MacArthur) term with all rates x3 (sim: 5.8 s at full light to 10.3 s at low light, light = period as intended), a floor because the cycle dips 27 dB, slow light noise against the LFO feel, and a sum instead of a mean so finger count matters. Fixed that way the held note is distinctive (bloom, bite click, dark sub-octave fungus hiss, recovery, shared across the chord); the Puls hit alone is a soft organ blip, its value is feeding the fungus of held notes - a real cross-lane idea that must cap the per-hit bite or a dense lane eats every alga to the floor.
